history.dynasty: Not established (12th-century origin per inscriptions; current shrine largely modern)
history.period: 12th century CE (per inscriptions); current structure modern
history.summary: Marudamalai is a hill temple of Lord Murugan atop a 600-foot hill in the Western Ghats, west of Coimbatore. The hill is also called Marudachalam and is believed to be a piece of the sacred Mount Meru; the hill is renowned as an abode of medicinal herbs. Inscriptions at the Thirumuruganathaswami Temple in Thirumuruganpoondi place the temple's origin in the 12th century CE, and it is counted among the Thirupugazh Sthalams and regarded as Muruga's seventh army camp (padaiveedu). Legend says a saint praying under a marudha tree was saved when water sprang from beneath it, and he hailed Muruga as 'Marudhajalapathi', which became 'Marudamalai'. The hill is also tied to Pambatti Siddhar, a former snake-charmer who meditated in a cave on its south-eastern slope (Pambatti Siddhar Kugai) and attained salvation there; the cave has a naturally formed snake image on the rock. Two springs on the hill, Marudha Thirtham and Pambatti Sunai, are believed to cure diseases through their medicinal properties. The current temple, built in the Dravidian style with a colourful gopuram, was developed in the 20th century with contributions from devotees including filmmaker M. M. A. Chinnappa Thevar, and the kumbabhishekam was performed in 1997.

name: Marudamalai Temple
town_description: Marudamalai is a village and hillock about 15 km west of Coimbatore on the foothills of the Western Ghats. The area is dominated by the herb-rich Marudamalai hill (Marudachalam), reached by a ghat road and by a flight of 837 steps from the base. The Pambatti Siddhar cave on the hill's south-eastern slope and the foothill shrine of Thaan Thondri Vinayagar are part of the pilgrimage circuit.

travel.airport: Coimbatore International Airport (approx. 30 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Coimbatore Junction (approx. 15 km), well connected across India.
travel.road: MTC buses run from Coimbatore city bus stands to the Marudamalai foothills; taxis and auto-rickshaws also ply. A ghat road leads up the hill, or devotees can climb the 837 steps to the shrine.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when the weather is cooler. Thai Poosam (January-February) is the most vibrant time to visit, with grand processions; visit early in the morning or in the evening to avoid the midday heat and crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 1:00 PM; evening 2:00 PM to 8:30 PM (closed 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM). Daily poojas: Vishwaroopa Darshan 6:00 AM, Kalasandhi 9:00 AM, Uchikalam 12:00 noon, Sayaratchai 5:00 PM, Arthajama 8:30 PM. Entry is free; small charges apply for special darshan and pooja tickets.
